facts.text: On this date in 1793, Marie Antoinette was executed — yet her hair had turned entirely white overnight after her arrest, a condition now known as Marie Antoinette syndrome, or acute stress-induced canities.
On this date in 1946, ten Nazi leaders were hanged at Nuremberg. Hermann Göring cheated the gallows by hours, crushing a cyanide capsule in his cell the night before.

Monaco has more millionaires per capita than any country on Earth — roughly one in three residents — yet it maintains no income tax and fits its entire population into an area smaller than Central Park.

The Philippines is the only country in the world that dissolves more marriages than it grants divorces, because divorce remains illegal there; annulment, a lengthier legal process, is the only exit from marriage.

Lagos is growing faster than almost any megacity in history. At current rates, it will surpass Cairo as Africa's largest city before 2030, housing more people than present-day Australia within a generation.
On this day in 1987, global markets were days from Black Monday — the Dow would shed 22.6% on Oct 19, still the largest single-day percentage drop in Wall Street history.
On this day in 2003, the NYSE ended its 211-year tradition of open-outcry specialist trading for most stocks, quietly handing the floor to electronic systems.
The S&P 500 has historically risen in the 12 months following a U.S. presidential election roughly 80% of the time, regardless of which party won.
Berkshire Hathaway's A-shares have never been split. One share, originally pennies in the 1960s, crossed $700,000 in 2024 — making it the most expensive stock ever listed.
The Dutch East India Company, the world's first publicly traded company, once had an inflation-adjusted market cap of roughly $8 trillion — dwarfing every modern corporation.

On this date in 1962, Kennedy received the first U-2 photographs of Soviet missiles in Cuba — a crisis partly resolved because light travels fast enough that a nuclear flash would have been seen before its shockwave arrived.
On October 16, 1846, ether was first used publicly as surgical anesthesia at Massachusetts General Hospital, ending millennia of patients being conscious during surgery.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city, making its surface gravity so intense that a marshmallow falling onto it would hit with the energy of a nuclear weapon.
Your body replaces roughly 330 billion cells every day — meaning in three months, most of you is materially newer than a season ago.
The universe is not only expanding but accelerating, which means distant galaxies are already receding faster than light, placing them permanently beyond any signal we could ever send.
On this day in 1793, Marie Antoinette was executed — 16 months after her husband, long enough to watch the Revolution devour itself.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. It predates Tenochtitlan by roughly 200 years.
On this day in 1916, Margaret Sanger opened America's first birth control clinic in Brooklyn. Police shut it down ten days later.
Woolly mammoths were still alive on Wrangel Island when the Egyptians were building the pyramids. The Stone Age and the Bronze Age overlapped in flesh and tusk.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was ancient history to the ancient Romans.
Saudade (Portuguese): a melancholic longing for something beloved and gone. Linguists consider it untranslatable — the word itself feels like the ache it names.
Kenopsia (n.): the eerie, forlorn atmosphere of a place usually bustling but now empty. Coined in 2012, it already feels ancient.
On this day in 1793, Marie Antoinette was executed — leaving behind a written apology to her lady-in-waiting for accidentally stepping on her executioner's foot. The word for that instinct: urbanity.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or never had. It collapses grief, nostalgia, and longing into a single breath.
On October 16, 1854, Abraham Lincoln delivered his Peoria Speech, deploying the word 'necessary' eleven times. Rhetoricians call such repetition anaphora — from Greek, meaning 'a carrying back'.

On this date in 2008, Satoshi Nakamoto published the Bitcoin whitepaper to a cryptography mailing list. Nine people replied. None realized they were reading the founding document of a $1 trillion asset class.
On Oct 16, 2023, Blackrock filed its spot Bitcoin ETF application for the second time — its first application had been rejected by the SEC eleven consecutive times across twelve years.

Ethereum's 2022 Merge reduced its energy consumption by ~99.95%, yet block times actually became more consistent: proof-of-stake slots are fixed at 12 seconds versus proof-of-work's probabilistic variance.

The Bitcoin genesis block contains an unspendable 50 BTC coinbase reward — not by design, but because Satoshi's original client didn't include genesis coinbase outputs in the UTXO set, locking them permanently.
MakerDAO's DAI maintained its $1 peg through a 45% ETH price crash in a single day in March 2020 — Black Thursday — though 4.5 million DAI was liquidated at $0 due to a gas auction failure.

On this date in 2015, OpenAI was formally incorporated — founded with a $1B pledge but launched with far less actual cash, by a group that included Musk and Altman explicitly trying to counter Google's dominance in AI.
On this date in 2017, Google Brain published 'Attention Is All You Need,' introducing the Transformer architecture that now underlies virtually every major language model in existence.

AlphaFold 2 predicted the structures of over 200 million proteins — nearly every known protein on Earth — in roughly a year, a task that would have taken the global scientific community millennia at prior experimental rates.

GPT-4 was trained on an estimated ~50 petaflop/s-days of compute; the human brain runs on roughly 20 watts and outperforms it on most open-ended reasoning tasks. The efficiency gap remains embarrassing for the silicon side.

The first neural network to defeat a professional Go player, AlphaGo, did so in 2016 — but the version that beat Lee Sedol was already obsolete within months, replaced by AlphaGo Zero, which learned solely from self-play with no human game data.
